summary.headline: Allcargo Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.2% YoY to INR546 crores and PAT turned to a INR14 crore profit from a Q1 FY26 loss.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR546 crores, up 11.2% YoY and 6.2% QoQ, with gross profit of INR163 crores (+11.6% YoY) and EBITDA of INR71 crores (+39.2% YoY). Express volumes grew 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes and realisation per tonne rose 6.4%, with management attributing much of the yield gain to natural escalation from service-quality improvement and only about 20% to diesel pass-through. Consultative Logistics revenue grew 6.1% YoY on a stable 7.5 million sq ft of warehouse space under management. Management reiterated a 3-year plan targeting Express EBITDA margin of 10% and a company-level EBITDA margin of about 13% this year.

financial_highlights.change: Within 28%-29% range over Q4 and Q1 per CFO
Includes about INR8 crores one-off from lease closure; normal run-rate about INR5 crores

segments.name: Express Logistics
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes; realisation per tonne up 6.4%; revenue up 13.5% YoY. Gross margin 26.3% and EBITDA margin about 6.2%, against a 10% three-year target.

segments.name: Consultative Logistics
segments.commentary: Warehouse space under management stable at 7.5 million sq ft; revenue up 6.1% YoY and 6.3% QoQ. Revenue per sq ft up 3%; EBITDA margin about 29.56%; customer retention 98%.

guidance_outlook: Company-level EBITDA margin expected around 13% for FY27, implying about 1 percentage point annual improvement over three years (confirmed by CFO).
Express EBITDA margin trajectory: 7.5% targeted this year and 10% in the three-year plan; management said it is 'inching up' from 6.2%.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin guided to 5%-6% this year and to improve thereafter.
Growth ambition: grow 1 percentage point above logistics industry growth; industry estimated at low double digits (1.2x-1.5x GDP of 6%-7%).
Price realisation actions expected to continue into Q2 FY27, with diesel pass-through impact seen fully from Q2.
Consultative Logistics revenue to grow slightly faster than Express, per management.
Capex: INR10-15 crores for Express infrastructure improvements; about INR20 crores additional capex for Consultative Logistics this year.
capex_capacity: Express: constant infrastructure improvements of INR10-15 crores; hubs described as well capitalised.
Consultative Logistics: about INR20 crores additional capex this year, tied to new business and warehouse additions.
Warehouse space under management at 7.5 million sq ft in Q1 FY27 (about 8 million sq ft earlier in the year per Q&A); two large warehouses were consolidated to reduce white space.
Express fleet and network: about 95% road and 5% air; capacity utilisation and lane planning cited as cost levers.
demand_pricing: Express realisation up 6.4% YoY; management attributes most (about 80%) to natural escalation from service-level improvement and about 20% to diesel pass-through, with DPH mechanism passed through since June.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage hikes is passed through in CL and Express contracts; annual GPI exercise applied.
Express KEA share about 60%-63% of revenue, retail about 20%, strategic balance; reclassification prevents direct comparison with earlier 80:20 split.
E-commerce and quick commerce: CL runs sort and fulfilment centres for majors; Express does not do last-mile for e-commerce.
Industry view: Express industry growth low double digits; shift from unorganised to organised players cited as a driver.
Q1 FY27 macro indicators cited: June e-way bills about 137 million (+14.5% YoY), GST collections near INR2 lakh crores (+14%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Express EBITDA margin and what are the levers to expand it?
qa_highlights.answer: Express EBITDA margin about 6.2% vs CL at 29.56%, giving the blended 13%. Yield enhancement is the main lever; cost and operating efficiency add further. Three-year target is 10%, with 7.5% targeted this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 24-month priorities and capital allocation policy after the demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth 1 percentage point above industry, with margin improvement across gross, EBITDA and PAT. Express is well capitalised (INR10-15 crores capex); CL needs about INR20 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Express gross margin base change versus earlier disclosures?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 figures reflected pre-merger Allcargo Gati numbers. Post the merger effective 1 November, prior quarters were recast to include CL aggregation, so the margin trajectory is around 30% from Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation increase is diesel versus natural escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the 6.3%-6.4% number precisely; roughly 80% natural escalation and 20% diesel pass-through. Diesel pass-through effective June, with full impact in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why has CL warehouse space declined over the last three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes are not impacted; two large warehouses were actioned to reduce white space, lowering cost without affecting revenue capability.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company focus more on CL given its margin and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both businesses get focus; CL revenue growth will be slightly faster than Express while balancing profitability of both.

risks_watch: Diesel and labour cost inflation: pass-through lags may compress margins in Q2 before full recovery.
Express EBITDA margin at about 6.2% remains far below the 10% three-year target; progress must be tracked quarterly.
Q1 PAT of INR14 crores includes about INR8 crores of one-off lease-closure income; underlying profit is lower.
CL warehouse area under management fell from about 8.4 million sq ft three quarters ago to 7.5 million sq ft; monitor volume impact.
Pre-Ind AS operating PBT margin of about 2.7% (per analyst) needs to reach 5%-6% this year.
Segment disclosure: analysts requested air/surface split and pre- vs post-Ind AS EBITDA bridge; not provided on the call. KEA classification changed, so historic comparisons are limited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume, pricing and CL retention, with a clear 3-year margin plan. Evasive on the KEA/strategic reclassification and on the exact diesel versus natural-escalation split, and it did not provide a segment EBITDA bridge.
key_quotes: Promised service quality delivered drives volume and when consistently delivered every day, it earns the right to command the right yield or the price.
That discipline has delivered a 6.4% year-on-year improvement in yield for the quarter.
We closed the quarter with service quality adherence of over 99%, and that consistency has led to a 98% customer retention rate.
So Express is at 6.2% and at CL, we are at Consultative Logistics, we are at 29.56%.
Both businesses will get the relevant focus from the organization with a clearer focus in terms of revenue growth, which will be a tad faster than Express on the CL side.

adds.what: Express infrastructure improvements (INR10-15 crores capex, no discrete capacity numbers given)
Consultative Logistics additional warehouse additions tied to new business (about INR20 crores capex this year, no sq ft figure given)

growth.why: Management guides Express EBITDA margin to 7.5% this year (10% in three-year plan) and consolidated EBITDA margin around 13%, with growth 1 percentage point above industry; backing is partial, relying mainly on price realisation, diesel pass-through, cost levers and modest capex (INR10-15 crores Express, about INR20 crores CL) with no specific capacity or order numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, with Express EBITDA margin 7.5% targeted
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA rose 39.2% YoY to INR71 crores, Express EBITDA margin is about 6.2% vs 7.5% FY27 target and 10% three-year target, and yield gains plus cost levers are the stated drivers, though diesel pass-through lags could compress Q2 margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or hub capacity with a date was guided; Express capex is only INR10-15 crores of infrastructure improvements and CL warehouse space fell from about 8.4 million sq ft to 7.5 million sq ft over three quarters.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Express volumes grew 6.7% YoY to 312,000 tonnes and management guides growth 1 percentage point above an industry growing at low double digits, with CL revenue growing slightly faster than Express, though CL space under management fell and retention is 98%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; capex is limited to about INR10-15 crores for Express and about INR20 crores for CL this year, with no board-level plant plan, so a major new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance (Express EBITDA 7.5%, consolidated EBITDA about 13%, pre-Ind AS PBT margin 5-6%) and Q1 PAT of INR14 crores includes about INR8 crores one-off lease income, so underlying profit is weaker than headline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Diesel pass-through impact only seen fully from Q2 and labour cost inflation lags pass-through, while the pre-Ind AS PBT margin was about 2.7% per analyst against a 5-6% target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or service launch was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Price realisation and diesel pass-through continuing into Q2
rows.why: Express realisation per tonne rose 6.4% YoY with about 20% from diesel pass-through (effective June), and management said price realisation actions continue into Q2 with full diesel impact from Q2.

rows.label: Post-demerger capital allocation and growth ambition
rows.why: Management described a 24-month priority of growing 1 percentage point above industry with margin improvement across gross, EBITDA and PAT, though no specific capital allocation numbers were given beyond the capex lines.

rows.label: Warehouse consolidation to cut white-space cost in CL
rows.why: Two large warehouses were consolidated, cutting space under management from about 8.4 million sq ft to 7.5 million sq ft, with management saying revenue capability is unaffected and CL EBITDA margin held at 29.56%.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, pricing, 98% CL retention and the 3-year margin plan, but cautious and evasive on the KEA reclassification, the diesel vs natural-escalation split and the segment EBITDA bridge; analysts pressed on those points and on the falling CL warehouse footprint.
